notes: inherent: The inherent vowel is a and is always said, so it is always typed (ಅಮ್ಮ amma, ಕನ್ನಡ kannada): there is no schwa deletion. Native words end in a vowel (ಮನೆ mane, ಮಾಡು maadu); a word ends in a virama only in loanwords (ಬಸ್ bas). anusvara: ಂ is the nasal of the stop after it inside a word (ಅಂದರೆ andare, ಸಂಬಂಧ sambandha, ತುಂಬಾ tumba). The tables have one spelling list for it wherever it stands, so the skeleton makes both readings one key: m before a consonant folds to n (the m + consonant entries of `replace`). A final n or m after a vowel is dropped (dropTrailing), for the rare final anusvara and for loanwords typed with or without their last nasal; on the calibration pairs it raised the skeleton from 96.2% to 96.5%. The price: a word that ends in n or m shares its key with the word without it. dentals: ತ is typed t or th (ತುಂಬಾ tumba / thumba, ತಿಳಿ tili / thili) and ದ d or dh; ಟ and ಡ are t and d. The skeleton folds th to t and dh to d, so ತ ಥ ಟ ಠ are one key letter, and ದ ಧ ಡ ಢ another. vowels: Long vowels are typed doubled about half the time (ನಾನು naanu / nanu, ಬೇಡ beda / beeda); ೇ and ೋ are mostly plain e and o. The skeleton folds aa, ee, ii, oo, uu, and ae and ea to e. letters: ಚ is ch, ಛ ch or chh, ಶ sh or s, ಷ sh, ಫ ph or f, ವ v or w, ಳ and ಲ l, ಣ and ನ n, ಱ and ರ r. ಋ and ೃ are ru (ಕೃಷ್ಣ krushna) or ri (krishna). ಕ್ಷ is ksh, ಜ್ಞ gn, jn or gy (ಜ್ಞಾನ gnana, jnana), ಶ್ರ shr or sr. The nukta letters ಜ಼ and ಫ಼ are z and f. doubled: Doubled consonants are common and usually typed doubled (ಅಕ್ಕ akka, ಇಲ್ಲ illa); ಚ್ಚ is cch, chch or ch (ಹೆಚ್ಚು hecchu), ತ್ತ tt or tth (ಮತ್ತು mattu / matthu), ದ್ದ dd or ddh.
